extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) is a collection of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word when exposed to the whole passage but not when only seeing the last sentence. It is designed to evaluate computational models' ability to understand broad discourse context.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández; CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were sourced from the BookCorpus, filtered by automated language models to remove easy examples, then evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower crowdsourcing in a three-step process: (1) one subject guesses the target word from the whole passage; (2) a second subject guesses from the whole passage; (3) multiple subjects attempt to guess from the target sentence only, up to 10 unsuccessful guesses.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels. After duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material, the corpus contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material using a stop word list. Passages where the target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of four language models were excluded. Novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects annotated passages via CrowdFlower in three steps: (1) one subject guessed the target word from the whole passage; if correct, (2) a second subject guessed from the whole passage; if also correct, (3) additional subjects tried to guess from the target sentence only, up to 10 unsuccessful guesses. Subjects in step 3 were allowed 3 guesses per sentence. Only passages passing all three steps were included.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: In the crowdsourcing pipeline, 84–86% of items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2, and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all selection steps.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 successful guesses from the broad context (steps 1 and 2), plus up to 10 unsuccessful guesses from the sentence-only context (step 3)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) (Mikolov et al., 2011), standard 4-gram model, RNN trained on BookCorpus, feed-forward model trained on BookCorpus — used as automated filters to exclude easy passages
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are publicly available for download. The test set will be made available at the time of a planned public competition.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Most target words in LAMBADA are proper nouns (48%), which are hugely overrepresented compared to the input data distribution. The dataset also contains direct speech significantly more often than the input items (71% vs. 61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset uses a strict hit-or-miss approach requiring exact word matches, excluding plausible synonymous continuations. The filtering process used language models that may introduce biases. The dataset is limited to narrative/novel text from BookCorpus, which may not generalize to other genres.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking of language models and computational models for text understanding, specifically evaluating broad discourse context understanding. The development set can be used to fine-tune models. Training data (raw BookCorpus text) is provided for training language models.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.

Any passage whose target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of the language models was excluded.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For a given passage, 1. one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage (comprising the context and the target sentence); if the guess was right, 2. a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if that guess was also right, 3. more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10; if no subject was able to guess the target word, the passage was added to the LAMBADA dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: A random sample of the remaining passages were then evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: In the crowdsourcing pipeline, 84–86% items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2 and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all the selection steps.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage... a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage... more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We used a combination of four language models, chosen by availability and/or ease of training: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) (Mikolov et al., 2011) and three models trained on the Book Corpus (a standard 4-gram model, a RNN and a feed-forward model)

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The development set of LAMBADA, along with the training corpus, can be downloaded at http://clic.cimec.unitn.it/lambada/. The test set will be made available at the time of the competition.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: most target words in LAMBADA are proper nouns (48%), followed by common nouns (37%) and, at a distance, verbs (7.7%). In fact, proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA, while the other categories are under-represented, compared to the POS distribution in the input.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: An alternative to this perfect-match approach would have been to include passages where broad-context subjects provided other plausible or synonymous continuations. However, it is very challenging, both practically and methodologically, to determine which answers other than the original fit the passage well

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We thus propose LAMBADA as a challenging test set, meant to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text... The development data can be used to fine-tune models to the specifics of the LAMBADA passages.
